bull.t: Low leverage and expanding capital base
bull.b: Minimal debt reduces financial risk and interest burdens, preserving flexibility while Dianthus funds clinical development. The expanded equity and asset base can support continued research and operations, giving the company a stronger foundation than a similarly loss-making biotech with heavy leverage.

The interim Phase 3 response signal supports meaningful progress for the lead program and could strengthen the path toward a future therapy for severe autoimmune disease. Continued clinical validation would improve commercial credibility and create a clearer basis for advancing the complement-focused pipeline.

bull.t: Strong gross economics on existing revenue
bull.b: Very high gross margins indicate that the limited revenue generated has strong underlying economics before operating investment. If clinical programs eventually produce recurring product or partnership revenue, this margin profile could provide substantial contribution toward research spending and future corporate overhead.

bear.b: Cash usage is rising materially as development spending continues, increasing the capital required to reach clinical and regulatory milestones. Persistent negative operating and free cash flow can reduce financial flexibility over time and may force additional funding before the business generates dependable operating cash.

bear.t: Persistent operating losses and limited scale
bear.b: The company has not yet demonstrated an operating model capable of converting its programs into sustainable earnings. Substantial losses and limited revenue scale leave results highly dependent on successful development progress, while continued investment can keep profitability distant even if gross margins remain high.

Without marketed products or recurring commercial revenue, Dianthus must rely on capital markets and similar financing activities to fund operations. This dependence can increase dilution risk and makes long-term execution more sensitive to the timing and availability of external funding.
